references.text: In [ref:Joh 5:6|John 5:6], Jesus sees the man lying there and knows he has been sick for a long time. Jesus' knowledge of the man's long-term suffering shows his omniscience and care.
In [ref:Joh 9:1|John 9:1], Jesus meets a man who had been blind from birth – another example of someone afflicted by illness for a very long time, whom Jesus heals.
In [ref:Luk 13:11|Luke 13:11], a woman is mentioned who had suffered from a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years. Like the man at Bethesda, she had endured chronic illness before Jesus intervened.
In [ref:Apg 3:2|Acts 3:2], a man is described who had been lame from birth and was carried daily to the temple gate. Here too, it concerns a long-term disability healed by divine power.
In [ref:Apg 4:22|Acts 4:22], it is noted that the healed man was over forty years old – emphasizing the duration of his suffering, just as with the thirty-eight years in John 5:5.
In [ref:Apg 9:33-34|Acts 9:33–34], Peter heals Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years because he was paralyzed. Chronic illness healed instantly highlights God's power.

In [ref:Mark 9:21|Mark 9:21], Jesus asks the father of the possessed boy how long he has been like this. The answer "from childhood" emphasizes the duration of the suffering, as in the case of the man at Bethesda.
